answer: Latent overlap ledger. Each identity gets a random sparse probe vector, and the registry records a ridge regression of every new agent’s outputs against existing vectors. When two identities correlate above a fixed threshold across independent probes, the registry flags them as one source and quarantines both. Attackers must maintain a whisper of uncorrelated noise per duplicate, and each new identity raises the atlas of probes it must dodge, so the per-identity cost is a full independent probe budget plus detection risk.
